title: Why Black musicians had few instruments and sports
summary: He explains that Black people got organs and pianos late and lacked tennis and golf for the same reasons.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: See, but that's what it was, see. Because we would play -- and so now, improvising all these things like we would do it. And maybe -- just like many of our pieces we were supposed to have composed were nothing but the white Americans' Baptist hymns and ALL stuff like that. But we turned it around in such a way -- we put it to our, where we -- because we didn't have the instrumentation to do it otherwise. And a lot of times, like when we started the ring shouts and all those things, they had nothing but the bones. Later on they had the banjo. How many people could afford an organ or a piano. My people were way late. It was the generation before me before we had an organ.
And that, we had to pump that. And I was almost coming out of high school before we had the piano.

We didn't know anything about those things. And it's just like in sports. Today, very few tennis -- we don't have many tennis players or golf players. Not because we don't have the mentality to do that, but they haven't been brought up in those things, you see.
